Synopsis:
While following the caravan, together with the players are ambushed by a group of players. If they side with the drider after the combat resolves it will thank them.

Cluster Contexts:
- SCL_Drider_PlayersAmbush.json: The players have agreed to help the Harpers ambush a caravan of Absolute cultists and prisoners. You've just arrived at the ambush site - the mood is tense, words are spoken in harsh whispers. When the Caravan arrives there's a monsterous drider at its head, muttering to itself, talking to an imaginary queen/majesty that represents the voice of his God, The Absolute. The player can try to trick the drider into handing over its magic lantern (the Moonlantern - a glowing lantern hanging from the end of a staff), although that could leave the drider exposed to the worst effects of the curse. Will likely end in combat, either because you signaled the Harpers to spring their ambush or because the drider got suspicious and attacked.
- SCL_Drider_HarpersAndPlayersAmbush.json: The players have agreed to help the Harpers ambush a caravan of Absolute cultists and prisoners. You've just arrived at the ambush site - the mood is tense, words are spoken in harsh whispers. When the Caravan arrives there's a monsterous drider at its head, muttering to itself, talking to an imaginary queen/majesty that represents the voice of his God, The Absolute. The player can try to trick the drider into handing over its magic lantern (the Moonlantern - a glowing lantern hanging from the end of a staff), although that could leave the drider exposed to the worst effects of the curse. Will likely end in combat, either because you signaled the Harpers to spring their ambush or because the drider got suspicious and attacked.
- SCL_Drider_ThanksAfterAmbush.json: The scene follows the caravan ambush and the nearby fight with a drider—an episode in which the party could have started as cult allies, fought the drider, or even switched sides mid‑combat. Off‑screen Harpers and a coveted moonlantern are closing in and the area (near Moonrise Towers) is on high alert; Last Light Inn is marked as a nearby refuge. In this window Kar'niss and the party are linked by a whispered, cinematic mind‑meld (the narrator wonders if the Absolute’s voice is in the exchange), and Kar'niss is assessing whether the player is a turncoat, a true believer, or an infiltrator. The player’s replies here (professing loyalty to the Absolute or claiming to have infiltrated the Harpers) determine whether Kar'niss spares them and how Harpers will treat the group.
- SCL_Drider_CaravanAmbushed.json: Harpers ambush the caravan and the players. If this dialog succeeds on starting, the players can decide to fight the Harpers or change sides and help the ambushers fight the drider.
- SCL_Drider_Caravan_HalfOrcCaster.json: Player approaches Kansif (a stoic, honourable male half-orc) and Brawler Vez (a mouthy female goblin) after clearing a checkpoint and entering their camp in the Shadowcurse. They two Absolute cultists assume you're a True Soul sent by Minthara (which may or may not be true) and will ask if you brought the lyre needed to summon their guide through the darkness. If you have, you can play it and the drider will emerge. If you haven't, they can tell you where to find it.

context: You and the party helped Harpers set an ambush on a caravan of Absolute cultists and prisoners; a monstrous drider (Kar'niss) led the caravan and the encounter escalated into combat when the ambush began or the drider grew suspicious. Kar'niss speaks to an imagined “Majesty” (the Absolute) and can psychically link minds—this scene features a whispered, cinematic mind‑meld in which the drider probes the party. Kar'niss is assessing whether the player is a True Soul, a turncoat, or an infiltrator; the player’s answers here decide whether Kar'niss spares them and how the Harpers will treat the group. Off‑screen the fight has just resolved (the party may have fought the drider, fought the Harpers, or switched sides); if the players side with Kar'niss it will thank them.
